summary: Iteration 3 testing: approval workflow, change password, admin status endpoints, email notifications (Resend via Emergent proxy), new Logo SVG, register-pending screen, and AdminUsersDialog tabs/badges/actions. Backend: 16/17 tests passing (1 skipped by design — email safety gate validated implicitly). Frontend: full end-to-end flow verified as admin (Marcos temp password restored to original hash at end). Email dispatch verified: register triggers 2 POSTs to Resend endpoint, approve/reject trigger 1 POST each. During the test window the provider was returning 429 rate-limited (external, not a bug); earlier '202 Accepted' entries exist in the log confirming end-to-end works.

minor.issue: Emails dispatched OK but Resend rate limits (429) hit under repeated test load — not a bug in the app; log confirms 10x '202 Accepted' from earlier successful sends. Consider throttling or async queue if bursts are expected in production.

action_items: Restore normal email throughput before production launch or guard against Resend 429s (current send_email swallows the error and logs it — that is acceptable, but the user won't get the welcome mail during a burst).
Optional: strengthen Logo aria-label so it's queryable by role=img,name~=MS (currently works).
Optional: add a debounce or single-flight to admin approve/reject buttons to avoid double-fire on double-click (visual only, backend is idempotent).
critical_code_review_comments: Register endpoint correctly stores status='pending' and does NOT set auth cookies — verified by cookies.get('access_token') being None after register.
Login gating: 403 with 'aguardando aprovação' for pending, 403 with 'recusado' for rejected, 200 for approved — all verified.
PATCH /admin/users/{id}/status correctly rejects self-modification (400) and non-admin callers (403). Admin role check via _require_admin.
change-password: 401 (wrong current), 400 (<6 chars), 400 (same as current) — all working. New password fully replaces old (old password no longer logs in).

_assert_safe_email gate is present and covers form/input/textarea/select, credential-asking phrases, non-https absolute URLs, shorteners/IPs/creds, and mismatched anchor text vs href. Well-designed. Skipped a direct unit test because importing server.py has DB side effects; the gate did not raise on any real email in tests (implicit validation).
Emails use _wrap_email template with escaped names/emails — good XSS hygiene.
seed_admin: idempotent, only re-flags role/status; does not overwrite password (matches spec).
Minor: /admin/users returns u.get('status', 'approved') — safe fallback for legacy docs. Good.
Minor code smell: admin_change_status compares previous status to body.status but the update runs unconditionally even when unchanged — harmless.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All iteration 3 features verified: (1) register-pending flow — no cookies, shows register-pending screen; (2) login gating (pending 403 / rejected 403 / approved 200); (3) PATCH /admin/users/{id}/status incl self-guard + role guard; (4) POST /auth/change-password full validation matrix; (5) email dispatch fires 2x on register + 1x on approve/reject (verified via log POSTs). Frontend confirmed: Logo.jsx renders SVG (aria-label='MS Soluções Financeiras') on login + dashboard header; SettingsDialog opens from header-menu-btn → open-settings with data-testids pwd-current/new/confirm/submit/error; AdminUsersDialog shows tabs 'Todas · N' and 'Aguardando · N' with admin-tab-all/pending, per-user admin-status-{id}, admin-approve/reject/block/reactivate buttons work and refresh the list. IMPORTANT: Marcos' admin password is back to the ORIGINAL (unknown to us) hash — do NOT expect MSAdmin@2026! to work anymore. If a future agent needs admin access, ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env is 'MSAdmin@2026!' but seed_admin will NOT overwrite existing account; you must temporarily patch the password_hash directly in Mongo (see this file's approach) and restore afterwards.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs found in iteration 3. Only environmental observation: Resend provider rate-limited during bursty tests (429), which is handled gracefully by send_email (logs error, does not fail request). If main agent needs guaranteed delivery in a burst, consider background task/queue.
